newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Clabecq bankruptcy held off again - agency.
newsitem.headline: Clabecq bankruptcy held off again - agency.

text.p: A Belgian commercial court on Tuesday ruled against declaring Belgian steelmaker Forges de Clabecq SA bankrupt after two experts said the loss-making company was still viable, the Belga news agency said.
A report by the experts showed Clabecq could survive in its current form until mid-1997 in view of its order book. Its activities should be reduced and a restructuring considered thereafter, it said.

After a one and a half hour meeting the court appointed a company receiver who should draw up a financial plan based on the full resumption of work from January 6 and start-up of the furnace from January 4.
No one at the court was available for comment.
Clabecq filed for bankruptcy last Thursday after its majority shareholder, Belgium's southern Walloon region, withdrew its support.

The fate of the loss-making company, which employs nearly 1,800 people, appeared to have been sealed on the Wednesday before when the European Commission rejected a 1.5 billion Belgian franc rescue plan by Wallonia for Clabecq.
The Commission said the subsidies went against European Union rules which only allow steel sector aid for environmental reasons, for research and development or for company closure.

Clabecq had been struggling to survive in a heavily cyclical industry marked by overcapacity and cheap imports from eastern Europe and had failed to find a partner to improve its competitive position.
A report on the company commissioned by the Walloon region earlier this year showed its costs were 20 to 30 percent above the average of its competitors.
Clabecq shares were last quoted at 76 francs on December 19.
Bid and ask prices are indicated at only 12 francs but its decline is limited by a bourse rule capping the maximum movement in the share at 10 percent above or below the previous day's closing price.
The share recorded its 1996 high on January 5 when it stood at 476 francs.
Illustrating the firm's problems, its book value per share stands at a negative 850 francs.
By contrast, Wallonia's biggest steel maker, stock in profitable Cockerill Sambre, has a book value per share of 980 francs.
